name: lesson-dedupe
purpose: Keep a lessons file from silting up with restatements of lessons already recorded.
corpus: One candidate lesson, paired with the closest existing lesson.

state_schema.candidate: the lesson about to be written, in full
state_schema.closest_existing: the existing lesson that covers the most similar ground
state_schema.existing_name: the slug of that existing lesson

relation.instructions: How does the candidate relate to the existing lesson?

criteria.duplicate: the same lesson in different words; nothing new
criteria.extends: the same subject with a new cause, failure mode or procedure

states_procedure.instructions: Does the candidate say what to DO next time, and not only what happened?

durable.instructions: Will this still be worth following in six months, rather than being tied to one incident?

generality.instructions: How widely does the candidate apply?

states_procedure.below: rewrite with a procedure line before writing

durable.below: leave it in the task record, not the lessons file

relation.note: a choice, not a threshold: act on the label, and send a tie to a human
relation.calibration: PARTIALLY CALIBRATED 2026-09-19 on 22 candidate/neighbour pairs from the vault. WHAT HOLDS: on the 7 high-similarity pairs, where the candidate is a consolidation entry that absorbed its neighbour, the pack answered `extends` 6 times with p>=0.85 and `duplicate` once at p=0.57 - correct or defensible in all 7. WHAT WAS NOT MEASURED: the other 15 were labelled `new` from a LEXICAL SIMILARITY BAND rather than by reading, which is a proxy label and not ground truth. The pack called 9 of those 15 `extends`; reading 3 of the 9 found the pack right on 2 (two MSIX lessons from one session; two lessons about recorded state decaying) and arguable on 1. The headline 55 percent accuracy therefore measures the proxy, not the pack. No true DUPLICATE exists in the corpus, so that class is entirely unmeasured. A real calibration means reading all 44 bodies.

notes: Feed the closest existing lesson in, not the whole file: the judgment is a comparison of two texts, and a whole corpus in one state makes every answer worse. Calibration note: do not label candidate/neighbour pairs from a similarity score. Lexical overlap is the RETRIEVAL step that finds the neighbour; it says nothing about whether one lesson extends the other, and using it as the label inverts the thing being measured.
